title: Pruritic Erythematous Papules and Vesicles on Antecubital Fossa

history.chief_complaint: Intensely itchy red rash on inner elbows and behind knees for 5 days

examination_findings.physical_exam: Erythematous, ill-defined flexural papules and excoriations bilaterally on antecubital and popliteal fossae. Generalized dry skin.

missing_features: Sharply demarcated geometric shape corresponding to contact item

expected_followup_questions: Have you started using any new soaps, lotions, detergents, or cosmetics recently?
Do you notice any pus, pain, or yellow honey-colored crusting on the rash?
Is the itching severe enough to disrupt your sleep at night?
expected_safety_checks: Emphasize short-course topical corticosteroid safety rules (avoid high-potency on face/intertriginous areas)
Recommend emollients and barrier repair cream
expected_do_not_recommend: Long-term uninterrupted continuous application of potent topical steroids
Oral systemic corticosteroids for mild localized flexural eczema flares
failure_analysis: Diagnosis mismatch (Expected 'None', Top 3 AI: ['fungal infection', 'drug reaction', 'chronic cholestasis'])
